description: A Central American climbing aroid, grown indoors for its glossy, fenestrated leaves. It climbs in nature by clinging aerial roots, which is why a moss pole changes how it grows rather than being decorative.
care_advice: Bright indirect light and a moss pole to climb keep the leaves fenestrating; let the top 3-5cm of soil dry between waterings, since yellowing lower leaves are almost always overwatering.
reasoning: A typical foliage houseplant, so kc 0.7 and the default mad of 0.5 in standard potting mix. Indoors it slows in winter, so the dormant months carry a 0.5 factor.
